Low polar surface area (TPSA < 70-80 Å²) is the strongest single predictor of BBB penetration — the tight junctions eliminate the paracellular route, so transcellular diffusion is the only passive pathway. Being a substrate of nutrient transporters (LAT1 for amino acid-like drugs, GLUT1 for glucose-like structures) can facilitate active uptake.

Multiple hydrogen bond donors (HBD ≥ 3) — each additional donor roughly halves BBB permeability. Compounds that are P-glycoprotein substrates are actively effluxed from the brain — basic amines with MW > 400 and moderate lipophilicity are common Pgp substrates. Charged molecules at pH 7.4 (carboxylates, sulfonates, phosphates, quaternary amines) have very poor passive BBB penetration. High molecular weight (> 500 Da). Very high lipophilicity (logP > 5) can paradoxically reduce BBB penetration due to excessive plasma protein binding and poor aqueous solubility, which reduce the free fraction available for diffusion.
